## Findings
- claim-1: For bigrassmannian \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) with \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), the two Schur intervals generate \(J_v\), and each has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. [source-2@L1382-L1421|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: In the square family \(n=4m,\ r=n-r=2m,\ i=j=m\), one has \(a=b=m\) and the generator count is \(\binom{2m}{m}\). Thus \(m=1\) gives two-element sets \(\{s_1,s_2\}\) and \(\{s_1,s_{11}\}\); \(m=2\) gives six-element sets \(\{s_{22},s_{32},s_{33},s_{42},s_{43},s_{44}\}\) and \(\{s_{22},s_{221},s_{2211},s_{222},s_{2221},s_{2222}\}\). [source-2@L1394-L1421|claim=formal-document] [source-2@L1508-L1515|claim=formal-document]
- claim-3: These \(m=1,2\) cases lie in the authors’ reported finite verification range \(r\le4,\ n-r\le5\), so they support, but do not prove, minimality. [source-2@L1501-L1502|claim=formal-document]
- claim-4: The next square case \(m=3\) has \(n=12,\ r=n-r=6,\ i=j=3,\ a=b=3\), hence two generating sets of \(20=\binom63\) elements. It lies outside the reported verification range; its minimality remains conjectural. [source-2@L1394-L1421|claim=formal-document] [source-2@L1501-L1502|claim=formal-document] [source-2@L1508-L1515|claim=formal-document]
- claim-5: The general assertion that all inclusion-minimal homogeneous generating sets have a common cardinality is false under the stated graded-algebra hypotheses: let \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z[x]/(x^2,6x)\), \(\deg x=1\), and \(M=(x)\). Then \(\Lambda_+M=0\), while both \(\{x\}\) and \(\{2x,3x\}\) are inclusion-minimal homogeneous generating sets of \(M\), of sizes \(1\) and \(2\); indeed \(x=2(2x)-3x\), whereas neither \(2x\) nor \(3x\) alone generates \(x\). This obstructs deriving common cardinality merely from the graded Nakayama criterion. [source-2@L1517-L1534|claim=formal-document]
- claim-6: Freeness \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\), if established, would rule out the preceding torsion obstruction and imply irredundance of either displayed family. The source records this only as a suspected statement. [source-2@L1536-L1552|claim=formal-document]
## Strategy
- Treat \(m=1,2,3\) as symbolic substitutions in the source’s interval formulas, not executed computations.
- Use \(m=1,2\) only as source-reported verified supporting cases; \(m=3\) is an explicit 20-generator test case unresolved in supplied evidence.
- Use the graded counterexample only to obstruct the general common-cardinality inference, not the \(J_v\) conjecture.
- Freeness of indecomposables, if proved, would establish irredundance of the two displayed families only.

## Gaps
- No executed computation or inspectable presentation/Smith-normal-form artifact for \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\), including \(m=3\), is supplied.
- Minimality for \(m=3\) is unresolved relative to supplied evidence.
- The source-reported verification has no independently inspectable computation artifact.
- Neither \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v)=\binom{a+b}{a}\) nor torsion-freeness is established.

## Next
- Form an integral Schur-multiplication presentation of \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\) for \(m=3\).
- Execute and preserve a bounded Smith-normal-form computation artifact.
- Compare its generator number and torsion with the predicted value \(20\); this would remain finite-case evidence only.
